title: Chemical Reactions and Balancing Equations (KS4 Chemistry)
subject: Chemistry
strapline: Conservation of mass and how to balance a symbol equation.
facts: In a chemical reaction, atoms are rearranged but never created or destroyed — this is conservation of mass.
Because no atoms are lost, the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products.
A balanced symbol equation has the same number of each type of atom on both sides.
You balance by placing big numbers (coefficients) in front of formulae — never by changing the small subscript numbers.
Example: H₂ + O₂ → H₂O is not balanced; 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O is.
A reaction where a substance gains oxygen is oxidation; losing oxygen is reduction.
Exothermic reactions release heat; endothermic reactions take in heat.

quick_quiz.q: In a reaction, is mass gained, lost, or conserved?
To balance an equation, what can you change — subscripts or the big numbers?
A reaction that releases heat is called what?

teacher_tips: Ban changing subscripts — the number-one balancing mistake.
Count atoms in a table under each side to check the balance.
Link conservation of mass to the "closed vs open system" mass practical.
